title: Seasonal Businesses and the Consistency Problem
content:
###  **The Two-Speed Business** 

Most home service companies operate at two speeds: overwhelmed and idle. Crews are turning away work in July and looking for something to do in February. 

Both states are expensive. Overwhelmed means turning down revenue and rushing jobs. Idle means paying for capacity that is not producing. 

###  **Why the Swing Is Usually Bigger Than It Needs to Be** 

A large part of the swing is self-inflicted. Marketing spend goes up when the phone is already ringing and gets cut when it goes quiet — which amplifies the peak and deepens the valley. 

###  **The Counter-Cyclical Approach** 

Companies that smooth the curve tend to do the opposite: they maintain or increase outreach during the slow months, when competition for homeowner attention is lowest and cost per conversation is effectively cheapest. 

Work booked in the off-season fills the front of the next busy season, which reduces the frantic scramble at the peak. 

###  **What Consistency Requires** 

This is difficult to do with an internal team, because slow months are exactly when payroll pressure makes cutting field staff most tempting. A weekly commitment that can be scaled up or down without hiring or firing anyone makes counter-cyclical outreach practical rather than theoretical.
